URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andraemon

Status Code: 200

Content:
Andraemon

In [Greek mythology](./Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](./Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](./Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](./Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](./Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](./Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](./Andraemon#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](./Andraemon#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](./Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](./Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](./Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](./Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](./Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](./Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](./Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](./Andraemon#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](./Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](./Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](./Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](./Andraemon#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](./Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](./Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](./Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](./Andraemon#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](./Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](./Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](./Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](./Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](./Andraemon#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](./Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](./Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](./Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](./Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](./Andraemon#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](./Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](./Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](./Andraemon#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](./Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](./Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](./Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](./Andraemon#cite_note-9)

***Apology for Smectymnuus***, or *An Apology for a Pamphlet*, was published by [John Milton](./John_Milton "John Milton") in April 1642. It was the final of his [antiprelatical tracts](./Milton's_antiprelatical_tracts "Milton's antiprelatical tracts") which criticize the structure of the [Church of England](./Church_of_England "Church of England").

Background
----------

The *[Apology](./Apologetics "Apologetics")* was published in April 1642 as *An Apology against a Pamphlet Called a Modest Confutation of the Animadversions upon the Remonstrant against Smectymnvvs* and is [his final antiprelatical tract](./Milton's_antiprelatical_tracts "Milton's antiprelatical tracts"). The tract was written as a response to a refutation by Bishop [Joseph Hall](./Joseph_Hall_(bishop) "Joseph Hall (bishop)").[[1]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-1)

Tract
-----

Milton argues that the defense of truth makes one vulnerable to personal attacks and emphasizes that role of personal integrity, especially his own:[[2]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-2) "as a member incorporate into that truth whereof I was perswaded".[[3]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-3) Milton defends his own integrity when he later writes:[[4]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-Wheeler_p._275-4) "that indeed according to art is most eloquent, which returns and approaches neerest to nature from whence it came; and they expresse nature best, who in their lives least wander from her safe leading, which may be call'd regenerate reason".[[5]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-5) This idea is expanded further when he says:

> he who would not be frustrated of his hope to write well hereafter in laudable things, ought him selfe to bee a true Poem, that is, a composition, and patterne of the best and honourable things; not presuming to sing high praises of heroick men, or famous Cities, unlesse he have in himselfe the experience and the practice of all that which is praise-worthy.[[6]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-6)

Themes
------

The *Apology*, like many of Milton's other tracts, praises Parliament and emphasizes that they are reformers and the basis of the country.[[7]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-7) The tract also connects truth of words with the individual's character.[[4]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-Wheeler_p._275-4) Paul Stevens emphasizes that the tract reflects how "Milton's self is produced in the process of writing" and that his self is put through "a series of culturally approved *laterall* transformations".[[8]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-8) In particular, Elizabeth Wheeler points out that the tract contains "Milton's understanding of [Aristotle](./Aristotle "Aristotle")'s definition of man as a political animal. Heroism lies in the risk of changing and being changed in verbal exchange."[[9]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-9)

--------

* [Smectymnuus](./Smectymnuus "Smectymnuus")

-----

Andraemon

In [Greek mythology](./Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](./Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](./Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](./Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](./Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](./Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](./Andraemon#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](./Andraemon#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](./Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](./Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](./Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](./Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](./Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](./Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](./Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](./Andraemon#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](./Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](./Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](./Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](./Andraemon#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](./Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](./Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](./Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](./Andraemon#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](./Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](./Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](./Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](./Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](./Andraemon#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](./Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](./Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](./Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](./Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](./Andraemon#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](./Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](./Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](./Andraemon#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](./Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](./Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](./Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](./Andraemon#cite_note-9)

***Apology for Smectymnuus***, or *An Apology for a Pamphlet*, was published by [John Milton](./John_Milton "John Milton") in April 1642. It was the final of his [antiprelatical tracts](./Milton's_antiprelatical_tracts "Milton's antiprelatical tracts") which criticize the structure of the [Church of England](./Church_of_England "Church of England").

Background
----------

The *[Apology](./Apologetics "Apologetics")* was published in April 1642 as *An Apology against a Pamphlet Called a Modest Confutation of the Animadversions upon the Remonstrant against Smectymnvvs* and is [his final antiprelatical tract](./Milton's_antiprelatical_tracts "Milton's antiprelatical tracts"). The tract was written as a response to a refutation by Bishop [Joseph Hall](./Joseph_Hall_(bishop) "Joseph Hall (bishop)").[[1]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-1)

Tract
-----

Milton argues that the defense of truth makes one vulnerable to personal attacks and emphasizes that role of personal integrity, especially his own:[[2]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-2) "as a member incorporate into that truth whereof I was perswaded".[[3]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-3) Milton defends his own integrity when he later writes:[[4]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-Wheeler_p._275-4) "that indeed according to art is most eloquent, which returns and approaches neerest to nature from whence it came; and they expresse nature best, who in their lives least wander from her safe leading, which may be call'd regenerate reason".[[5]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-5) This idea is expanded further when he says:

> he who would not be frustrated of his hope to write well hereafter in laudable things, ought him selfe to bee a true Poem, that is, a composition, and patterne of the best and honourable things; not presuming to sing high praises of heroick men, or famous Cities, unlesse he have in himselfe the experience and the practice of all that which is praise-worthy.[[6]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-6)

Themes
------

The *Apology*, like many of Milton's other tracts, praises Parliament and emphasizes that they are reformers and the basis of the country.[[7]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-7) The tract also connects truth of words with the individual's character.[[4]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-Wheeler_p._275-4) Paul Stevens emphasizes that the tract reflects how "Milton's self is produced in the process of writing" and that his self is put through "a series of culturally approved *laterall* transformations".[[8]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-8) In particular, Elizabeth Wheeler points out that the tract contains "Milton's understanding of [Aristotle](./Aristotle "Aristotle")'s definition of man as a political animal. Heroism lies in the risk of changing and being changed in verbal exchange."[[9]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-9)

Andraemon

In [Greek mythology](./Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](./Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](./Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](./Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](./Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](./Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](./Andraemon#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](./Andraemon#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](./Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](./Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](./Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](./Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](./Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](./Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](./Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](./Andraemon#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](./Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](./Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](./Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](./Andraemon#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](./Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](./Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](./Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](./Andraemon#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](./Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](./Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](./Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](./Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](./Andraemon#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](./Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](./Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](./Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](./Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](./Andraemon#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](./Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](./Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](./Andraemon#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](./Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](./Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](./Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](./Andraemon#cite_note-9)

***Apology for Smectymnuus***, or *An Apology for a Pamphlet*, was published by [John Milton](./John_Milton "John Milton") in April 1642. It was the final of his [antiprelatical tracts](./Milton's_antiprelatical_tracts "Milton's antiprelatical tracts") which criticize the structure of the [Church of England](./Church_of_England "Church of England").

Background
----------

The *[Apology](./Apologetics "Apologetics")* was published in April 1642 as *An Apology against a Pamphlet Called a Modest Confutation of the Animadversions upon the Remonstrant against Smectymnvvs* and is [his final antiprelatical tract](./Milton's_antiprelatical_tracts "Milton's antiprelatical tracts"). The tract was written as a response to a refutation by Bishop [Joseph Hall](./Joseph_Hall_(bishop) "Joseph Hall (bishop)").[[1]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-1)

Tract
-----

Milton argues that the defense of truth makes one vulnerable to personal attacks and emphasizes that role of personal integrity, especially his own:[[2]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-2) "as a member incorporate into that truth whereof I was perswaded".[[3]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-3) Milton defends his own integrity when he later writes:[[4]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-Wheeler_p._275-4) "that indeed according to art is most eloquent, which returns and approaches neerest to nature from whence it came; and they expresse nature best, who in their lives least wander from her safe leading, which may be call'd regenerate reason".[[5]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-5) This idea is expanded further when he says:

> he who would not be frustrated of his hope to write well hereafter in laudable things, ought him selfe to bee a true Poem, that is, a composition, and patterne of the best and honourable things; not presuming to sing high praises of heroick men, or famous Cities, unlesse he have in himselfe the experience and the practice of all that which is praise-worthy.[[6]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-6)

Themes
------

The *Apology*, like many of Milton's other tracts, praises Parliament and emphasizes that they are reformers and the basis of the country.[[7]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-7) The tract also connects truth of words with the individual's character.[[4]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-Wheeler_p._275-4) Paul Stevens emphasizes that the tract reflects how "Milton's self is produced in the process of writing" and that his self is put through "a series of culturally approved *laterall* transformations".[[8]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-8) In particular, Elizabeth Wheeler points out that the tract contains "Milton's understanding of [Aristotle](./Aristotle "Aristotle")'s definition of man as a political animal. Heroism lies in the risk of changing and being changed in verbal exchange."[[9]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-9)

Andraemon

In [Greek mythology](./Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](./Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](./Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](./Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](./Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](./Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](./Andraemon#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](./Andraemon#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](./Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](./Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](./Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](./Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](./Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](./Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](./Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](./Andraemon#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](./Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](./Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](./Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](./Andraemon#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](./Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](./Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](./Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](./Andraemon#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](./Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](./Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](./Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](./Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](./Andraemon#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](./Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](./Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](./Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](./Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](./Andraemon#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](./Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](./Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](./Andraemon#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](./Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](./Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](./Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](./Andraemon#cite_note-9)

It was the final of his [antiprelatical tracts](./Milton\\'s_antiprelatical_tracts \"Milton\\'s antiprelatical tracts\") which criticize the structure of the [Church of England](./Church_of_England \"Church of England\").\\n\\nBackground\\n----------\\n\\nThe *[Apology](./Apologetics \"Apologetics\")* was published in April 1642 as *An Apology against a Pamphlet Called a Modest Confutation of the Animadversions upon the Remonstrant against Smectymnvvs* and is [his final antiprelatical tract](./Milton\\'s_antiprelatical_tracts \"Milton\\'s antiprelatical tracts\"). The tract was written as a response to a refutation by Bishop [Joseph Hall](./Joseph_Hall_(bishop) \"Joseph Hall (bishop)\").[[1]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-1)\\n\\nTract\\n-----\\n\\nMilton argues that the defense of truth makes one vulnerable to personal attacks and emphasizes that role of personal integrity, especially his own:[[2]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-2) \"as a member incorporate into that truth whereof I was perswaded\".[[3]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-3) Milton defends his own integrity when he later writes:[[4]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-Wheeler_p._275-4) \"that indeed according to art is most eloquent, which returns and approaches neerest to nature from whence it came; and they expresse nature best, who in their lives least wander from her safe leading, which may be call\\'d regenerate reason\".[[5]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-5) This idea is expanded further when he says:\\n\\n> he who would not be frustrated of his hope to write well hereafter in laudable things, ought him selfe to bee a true Poem, that is, a composition, and patterne of the best and honourable things; not presuming to sing high praises of heroick men, or famous Cities, unlesse he have in himselfe the experience and the practice of all that which is praise-worthy.[[6]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-6)\\n\\nThemes\\n------\\n\\nThe *Apology*, like many of Milton\\'s other tracts, praises Parliament and emphasizes that they are reformers and the basis of the country.[[7]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-7) The tract also connects truth of words with the individual\\'s character.[[4]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-Wheeler_p._275-4) Paul Stevens emphasizes that the tract reflects how \"Milton\\'s self is produced in the process of writing\" and that his self is put through \"a series of culturally approved *laterall* transformations\".[[8]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-8) In particular, Elizabeth Wheeler points out that the tract contains \"Milton\\'s understanding of [Aristotle](./Aristotle \"Aristotle\")\\'s definition of man as a political animal. Heroism lies in the risk of changing and being changed in verbal exchange.\"[[9]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-9)\\n\\nSee also\\n--------\\n\\n* [Smectymnuus](./Smectymnuus \"Smectymnuus\")\\n\\nNotes\\n-----\\n\\n1. |\\nURL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andraemon\\n\\nStatus Code: 200\\n\\nContent:\\nAndraemon\\n\\nIn [Greek mythology](./Greek_mythology \"Greek mythology\") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](./Help:IPA/English \"Help:IPA/English\"); [Ancient Greek](./Ancient_Greek_language \"Ancient Greek language\"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](./Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek \"Romanization of Ancient Greek\"):\\xa0*Andraímon*) may refer to:\\n\\n* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](./Oxylus \"Oxylus\") and husband of [Dryope](./Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) \"Dryope (daughter of Dryops)\").[[1]](./Andraemon#cite_note-1)\\n* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](./Andraemon#cite_note-2)\\n* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](./Aetolia \"Aetolia\") king and husband of [Gorge](./Gorge_(mythology) \"Gorge (mythology)\") of [Calydon](./Calydon \"Calydon\"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](./Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) \"Thoas (king of Aetoila)\"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](./Oeneus \"Oeneus\")\\' power over [Aetolia](./Aetolia \"Aetolia\"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](./Amfissa \"Amfissa\").[[3]](./Andraemon#cite_note-3)\\n* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](./Leonteus_(mythology) \"Leonteus (mythology)\"). He married [Amphinome](./Amphinome \"Amphinome\"), a daughter of [Pelias](./Pelias \"Pelias\").[[4]](./Andraemon#cite_note-4)\\n* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](./Suitors_of_Penelope \"Suitors of Penelope\") of [Penelope](./Penelope \"Penelope\") who came from [Dulichium](./Dulichium \"Dulichium\") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](./Andraemon#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](./Odysseus \"Odysseus\") with the aid of [Eumaeus](./Eumaeus \"Eumaeus\"), [Philoetius](./Philoetius_(Odyssey) \"Philoetius (Odyssey)\"), and [Telemachus](./Telemachus \"Telemachus\").[[6]](./Andraemon#cite_note-6)\\n* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](./Codrus \"Codrus\"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](./Asia_Minor \"Asia Minor\") and drove the [Carians](./Caria \"Caria\") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](./Colophon_(city) \"Colophon (city)\").[[7]](./Andraemon#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](./Mimnermus \"Mimnermus\") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](./Pylos \"Pylos\") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](./Andraemon#cite_note-8)\\n\\nSimilarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](./Patronymic \"Patronymic\"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](./Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) \"Thoas (king of Aetoila)\"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](./Gorge_(mythology) \"Gorge (mythology)\").[[9]](./Andraemon#cite_note-9)\\n\\nNotes\\n-----\\n\\n* ![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ad/Parthenon_from_west.jpg/40px-Parthenon_from_west.jpg)[Ancient Greece portal](./Portal:Ancient_Greece \"Portal:Ancient Greece\")\\n* ![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e9/Draig.svg/40px-Draig.svg.png)[Myths portal](./Portal:Myths \"Portal:Myths\")\\n\\n1. Andraemon

In [Greek mythology](./Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](./Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](./Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](./Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](./Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](./Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](./Andraemon#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](./Andraemon#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](./Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](./Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](./Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](./Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](./Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](./Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](./Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](./Andraemon#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](./Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](./Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](./Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](./Andraemon#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](./Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](./Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](./Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](./Andraemon#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](./Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](./Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](./Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](./Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](./Andraemon#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](./Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](./Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](./Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](./Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](./Andraemon#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](./Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](./Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](./Andraemon#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](./Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](./Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](./Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](./Andraemon#cite_note-9)

***Apology for Smectymnuus***, or *An Apology for a Pamphlet*, was published by [John Milton](./John_Milton "John Milton") in April 1642. It was the final of his [antiprelatical tracts](./Milton's_antiprelatical_tracts "Milton's antiprelatical tracts") which criticize the structure of the [Church of England](./Church_of_England "Church of England").

Background
----------

The *[Apology](./Apologetics "Apologetics")* was published in April 1642 as *An Apology against a Pamphlet Called a Modest Confutation of the Animadversions upon the Remonstrant against Smectymnvvs* and is [his final antiprelatical tract](./Milton's_antiprelatical_tracts "Milton's antiprelatical tracts"). The tract was written as a response to a refutation by Bishop [Joseph Hall](./Joseph_Hall_(bishop) "Joseph Hall (bishop)").[[1]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-1)

Tract
-----

Milton argues that the defense of truth makes one vulnerable to personal attacks and emphasizes that role of personal integrity, especially his own:[[2]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-2) "as a member incorporate into that truth whereof I was perswaded".[[3]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-3) Milton defends his own integrity when he later writes:[[4]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-Wheeler_p._275-4) "that indeed according to art is most eloquent, which returns and approaches neerest to nature from whence it came; and they expresse nature best, who in their lives least wander from her safe leading, which may be call'd regenerate reason".[[5]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-5) This idea is expanded further when he says:

> he who would not be frustrated of his hope to write well hereafter in laudable things, ought him selfe to bee a true Poem, that is, a composition, and patterne of the best and honourable things; not presuming to sing high praises of heroick men, or famous Cities, unlesse he have in himselfe the experience and the practice of all that which is praise-worthy.[[6]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-6)

Themes
------

The *Apology*, like many of Milton's other tracts, praises Parliament and emphasizes that they are reformers and the basis of the country.[[7]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-7) The tract also connects truth of words with the individual's character.[[4]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-Wheeler_p._275-4) Paul Stevens emphasizes that the tract reflects how "Milton's self is produced in the process of writing" and that his self is put through "a series of culturally approved *laterall* transformations".[[8]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-8) In particular, Elizabeth Wheeler points out that the tract contains "Milton's understanding of [Aristotle](./Aristotle "Aristotle")'s definition of man as a political animal. Heroism lies in the risk of changing and being changed in verbal exchange."[[9]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-9)

Andraemon

In [Greek mythology](./Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](./Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](./Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](./Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](./Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](./Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](./Andraemon#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](./Andraemon#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](./Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](./Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](./Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](./Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](./Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](./Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](./Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](./Andraemon#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](./Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](./Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](./Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](./Andraemon#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](./Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](./Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](./Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](./Andraemon#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](./Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](./Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](./Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](./Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](./Andraemon#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](./Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](./Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](./Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](./Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](./Andraemon#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](./Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](./Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](./Andraemon#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](./Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](./Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](./Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](./Andraemon#cite_note-9)

* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](./Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](./Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](./Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](./Andraemon#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](./Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](./Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](./Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](./Andraemon#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](./Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](./Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](./Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](./Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](./Andraemon#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](./Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](./Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](./Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](./Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](./Andraemon#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](./Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](./Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](./Andraemon#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](./Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](./Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](./Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](./Andraemon#cite_note-9)

***Apology for Smectymnuus***, or *An Apology for a Pamphlet*, was published by [John Milton](./John_Milton "John Milton") in April 1642. It was the final of his [antiprelatical tracts](./Milton's_antiprelatical_tracts "Milton's antiprelatical tracts") which criticize the structure of the [Church of England](./Church_of_England "Church of England").

Background
----------

The *[Apology](./Apologetics "Apologetics")* was published in April 1642 as *An Apology against a Pamphlet Called a Modest Confutation of the Animadversions upon the Remonstrant against Smectymnvvs* and is [his final antiprelatical tract](./Milton's_antiprelatical_tracts "Milton's antiprelatical tracts"). The tract was written as a response to a refutation by Bishop [Joseph Hall](./Joseph_Hall_(bishop) "Joseph Hall (bishop)").[[1]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-1)

Tract
-----

Milton argues that the defense of truth makes one vulnerable to personal attacks and emphasizes that role of personal integrity, especially his own:[[2]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-2) "as a member incorporate into that truth whereof I was perswaded".[[3]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-3) Milton defends his own integrity when he later writes:[[4]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-Wheeler_p._275-4) "that indeed according to art is most eloquent, which returns and approaches neerest to nature from whence it came; and they expresse nature best, who in their lives least wander from her safe leading, which may be call'd regenerate reason".[[5]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-5) This idea is expanded further when he says:

> he who would not be frustrated of his hope to write well hereafter in laudable things, ought him selfe to bee a true Poem, that is, a composition, and patterne of the best and honourable things; not presuming to sing high praises of heroick men, or famous Cities, unlesse he have in himselfe the experience and the practice of all that which is praise-worthy.[[6]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-6)

Themes
------

The *Apology*, like many of Milton's other tracts, praises Parliament and emphasizes that they are reformers and the basis of the country.[[7]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-7) The tract also connects truth of words with the individual's character.[[4]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-Wheeler_p._275-4) Paul Stevens emphasizes that the tract reflects how "Milton's self is produced in the process of writing" and that his self is put through "a series of culturally approved *laterall* transformations".[[8]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-8) In particular, Elizabeth Wheeler points out that the tract contains "Milton's understanding of [Aristotle](./Aristotle "Aristotle")'s definition of man as a political animal. Heroism lies in the risk of changing and being changed in verbal exchange."[[9]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-9)

Andraemon

In [Greek mythology](./Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](./Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](./Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](./Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](./Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](./Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](./Andraemon#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](./Andraemon#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](./Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](./Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](./Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](./Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](./Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](./Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](./Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](./Andraemon#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](./Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](./Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](./Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](./Andraemon#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](./Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](./Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](./Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](./Andraemon#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](./Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](./Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](./Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](./Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](./Andraemon#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](./Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](./Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](./Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](./Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](./Andraemon#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](./Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](./Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](./Andraemon#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](./Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](./Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](./Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](./Andraemon#cite_note-9)

Please improve this article by adding [secondary or tertiary sources](./Wikipedia:No_original_research#Primary,_secondary_and_tertiary_sources \"Wikipedia:No original research\").  *Find sources:*\\xa0[\"Apology for Smectymnuus\"](https://www.google.com/search?as_eq=wikipedia&q=%22Apology+for+Smectymnuus%22)\\xa0–\\xa0[news](https://www.google.com/search?tbm=nws&q=%22Apology+for+Smectymnuus%22+-wikipedia&tbs=ar:1)\\xa0**·** [newspapers](https://www.google.com/search?&q=%22Apology+for+Smectymnuus%22&tbs=bkt:s&tbm=bks)\\xa0**·** [books](https://www.google.com/search?tbs=bks:1&q=%22Apology+for+Smectymnuus%22+-wikipedia)\\xa0**·** [scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22Apology+for+Smectymnuus%22)\\xa0**·** [JSTOR](https://www.jstor.org/action/doBasicSearch?Query=%22Apology+for+Smectymnuus%22&acc=on&wc=on) *(December 2023)* *([Learn how and when to remove this message](./Help:Maintenance_template_removal \"Help:Maintenance template removal\"))* |\\n\\n***Apology for Smectymnuus***, or *An Apology for a Pamphlet*, was published by [John Milton](./John_Milton \"John Milton\") in April 1642. It was the final of his [antiprelatical tracts](./Milton\\'s_antiprelatical_tracts \"Milton\\'s antiprelatical tracts\") which criticize the structure of the [Church of England](./Church_of_England \"Church of England\").\\n\\nBackground\\n----------\\n\\nThe *[Apology](./Apologetics \"Apologetics\")* was published in April 1642 as *An Apology against a Pamphlet Called a Modest Confutation of the Animadversions upon the Remonstrant against Smectymnvvs* and is [his final antiprelatical tract](./Milton\\'s_antiprelatical_tracts \"Milton\\'s antiprelatical tracts\"). The tract was written as a response to a refutation by Bishop [Joseph Hall](./Joseph_Hall_(bishop) \"Joseph Hall (bishop)\").[[1]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-1)\\n\\nTract\\n-----\\n\\nMilton argues that the defense of truth makes one vulnerable to personal attacks and emphasizes that role of personal integrity, especially his own:[[2]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-2) \"as a member incorporate into that truth whereof I was perswaded\".[[3]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-3) Milton defends his own integrity when he later writes:[[4]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-Wheeler_p._275-4) \"that indeed according to art is most eloquent, which returns and approaches neerest to nature from whence it came; and they expresse nature best, who in their lives least wander from her safe leading, which may be call\\'d regenerate reason\".[[5]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-5) This idea is expanded further when he says:\\n\\n> he who would not be frustrated of his hope to write well hereafter in laudable things, ought him selfe to bee a true Poem, that is, a composition, and patterne of the best and honourable things; not presuming to sing high praises of heroick men, or famous Cities, unlesse he have in himselfe the experience and the practice of all that which is praise-worthy.[[6]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-6)\\n\\nThemes\\n------\\n\\nThe *Apology*, like many of Milton\\'s other tracts, praises Parliament and emphasizes that they are reformers and the basis of the country.[[7]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-7) The tract also connects truth of words with the individual\\'s character.[[4]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-Wheeler_p._275-4) Paul Stevens emphasizes that the tract reflects how \"Milton\\'s self is produced in the process of writing\" and that his self is put through \"a series of culturally approved *laterall* transformations\".[[8]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-8) In particular, Elizabeth Wheeler points out that the tract contains \"Milton\\'s understanding of [Aristotle](./Aristotle \"Aristotle\")\\'s definition of man as a political animal. Heroism lies in the risk of changing and being changed in verbal exchange.\"[[9]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-9)\\n\\nSee also\\n--------\\n\\n* [Smectymnuus](./Smectymnuus \"Smectymnuus\")\\n\\nNotes\\n-----\\n\\n1. |\\nURL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andraemon\\n\\nStatus Code: 200\\n\\nContent:\\nAndraemon\\n\\nIn [Greek mythology](./Greek_mythology \"Greek mythology\") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](./Help:IPA/English \"Help:IPA/English\"); [Ancient Greek](./Ancient_Greek_language \"Ancient Greek language\"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](./Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek \"Romanization of Ancient Greek\"):\\xa0*Andraímon*) may refer to:\\n\\n* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](./Oxylus \"Oxylus\") and husband of [Dryope](./Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) \"Dryope (daughter of Dryops)\").[[1]](./Andraemon#cite_note-1)\\n* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](./Andraemon#cite_note-2)\\n* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](./Aetolia \"Aetolia\") king and husband of [Gorge](./Gorge_(mythology) \"Gorge (mythology)\") of [Calydon](./Calydon \"Calydon\"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](./Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) \"Thoas (king of Aetoila)\"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](./Oeneus \"Oeneus\")\\' power over [Aetolia](./Aetolia \"Aetolia\"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](./Amfissa \"Amfissa\").[[3]](./Andraemon#cite_note-3)\\n* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](./Leonteus_(mythology) \"Leonteus (mythology)\"). He married [Amphinome](./Amphinome \"Amphinome\"), a daughter of [Pelias](./Pelias \"Pelias\").[[4]](./Andraemon#cite_note-4)\\n* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](./Suitors_of_Penelope \"Suitors of Penelope\") of [Penelope](./Penelope \"Penelope\") who came from [Dulichium](./Dulichium \"Dulichium\") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](./Andraemon#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](./Odysseus \"Odysseus\") with the aid of [Eumaeus](./Eumaeus \"Eumaeus\"), [Philoetius](./Philoetius_(Odyssey) \"Philoetius (Odyssey)\"), and [Telemachus](./Telemachus \"Telemachus\").[[6]](./Andraemon#cite_note-6)\\n* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](./Codrus \"Codrus\"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](./Asia_Minor \"Asia Minor\") and drove the [Carians](./Caria \"Caria\") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](./Colophon_(city) \"Colophon (city)\").[[7]](./Andraemon#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](./Mimnermus \"Mimnermus\") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](./Pylos \"Pylos\") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](./Andraemon#cite_note-8)\\n\\nSimilarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](./Patronymic \"Patronymic\"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](./Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) \"Thoas (king of Aetoila)\"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](./Gorge_(mythology) \"Gorge (mythology)\").[[9]](./Andraemon#cite_note-9)\\n\\nNotes\\n-----\\n\\n* ![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ad/Parthenon_from_west.jpg/40px-Parthenon_from_west.jpg)[Ancient Greece portal](./Portal:Ancient_Greece \"Portal:Ancient Greece\")\\n* ![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e9/Draig.svg/40px-Draig.svg.png)[Myths portal](./Portal:Myths \"Portal:Myths\")\\n\\n1. Andraemon

In [Greek mythology](./Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](./Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](./Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](./Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](./Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](./Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](./Andraemon#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](./Andraemon#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](./Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](./Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](./Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](./Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](./Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](./Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](./Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](./Andraemon#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](./Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](./Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](./Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](./Andraemon#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](./Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](./Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](./Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](./Andraemon#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](./Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](./Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](./Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](./Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](./Andraemon#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](./Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](./Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](./Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](./Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](./Andraemon#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](./Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](./Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](./Andraemon#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](./Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](./Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](./Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](./Andraemon#cite_note-9)

Andraemon

In [Greek mythology](./Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](./Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](./Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](./Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](./Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](./Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](./Andraemon#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](./Andraemon#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](./Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](./Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](./Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](./Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](./Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](./Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](./Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](./Andraemon#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](./Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](./Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](./Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](./Andraemon#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](./Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](./Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](./Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](./Andraemon#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](./Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](./Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](./Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](./Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](./Andraemon#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](./Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](./Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](./Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](./Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](./Andraemon#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](./Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](./Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](./Andraemon#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](./Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](./Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](./Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](./Andraemon#cite_note-9)

***Apology for Smectymnuus***, or *An Apology for a Pamphlet*, was published by [John Milton](./John_Milton "John Milton") in April 1642. It was the final of his [antiprelatical tracts](./Milton's_antiprelatical_tracts "Milton's antiprelatical tracts") which criticize the structure of the [Church of England](./Church_of_England "Church of England").

Background
----------

The *[Apology](./Apologetics "Apologetics")* was published in April 1642 as *An Apology against a Pamphlet Called a Modest Confutation of the Animadversions upon the Remonstrant against Smectymnvvs* and is [his final antiprelatical tract](./Milton's_antiprelatical_tracts "Milton's antiprelatical tracts"). The tract was written as a response to a refutation by Bishop [Joseph Hall](./Joseph_Hall_(bishop) "Joseph Hall (bishop)").[[1]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-1)

Tract
-----

Milton argues that the defense of truth makes one vulnerable to personal attacks and emphasizes that role of personal integrity, especially his own:[[2]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-2) "as a member incorporate into that truth whereof I was perswaded".[[3]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-3) Milton defends his own integrity when he later writes:[[4]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-Wheeler_p._275-4) "that indeed according to art is most eloquent, which returns and approaches neerest to nature from whence it came; and they expresse nature best, who in their lives least wander from her safe leading, which may be call'd regenerate reason".[[5]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-5) This idea is expanded further when he says:

> he who would not be frustrated of his hope to write well hereafter in laudable things, ought him selfe to bee a true Poem, that is, a composition, and patterne of the best and honourable things; not presuming to sing high praises of heroick men, or famous Cities, unlesse he have in himselfe the experience and the practice of all that which is praise-worthy.[[6]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-6)

Themes
------

The *Apology*, like many of Milton's other tracts, praises Parliament and emphasizes that they are reformers and the basis of the country.[[7]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-7) The tract also connects truth of words with the individual's character.[[4]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-Wheeler_p._275-4) Paul Stevens emphasizes that the tract reflects how "Milton's self is produced in the process of writing" and that his self is put through "a series of culturally approved *laterall* transformations".[[8]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-8) In particular, Elizabeth Wheeler points out that the tract contains "Milton's understanding of [Aristotle](./Aristotle "Aristotle")'s definition of man as a political animal. Heroism lies in the risk of changing and being changed in verbal exchange."[[9]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-9)

Andraemon

In [Greek mythology](./Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](./Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](./Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](./Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](./Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](./Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](./Andraemon#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](./Andraemon#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](./Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](./Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](./Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](./Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](./Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](./Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](./Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](./Andraemon#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](./Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](./Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](./Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](./Andraemon#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](./Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](./Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](./Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](./Andraemon#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](./Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](./Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](./Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](./Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](./Andraemon#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](./Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](./Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](./Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](./Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](./Andraemon#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](./Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](./Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](./Andraemon#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](./Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](./Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](./Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](./Andraemon#cite_note-9)

Andraemon

In [Greek mythology](./Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](./Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](./Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](./Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](./Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](./Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](./Andraemon#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](./Andraemon#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](./Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](./Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](./Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](./Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](./Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](./Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](./Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](./Andraemon#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](./Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](./Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](./Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](./Andraemon#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](./Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](./Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](./Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](./Andraemon#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](./Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](./Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](./Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](./Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](./Andraemon#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](./Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](./Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](./Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](./Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](./Andraemon#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](./Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](./Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](./Andraemon#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](./Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](./Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](./Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](./Andraemon#cite_note-9)

***Apology for Smectymnuus***, or *An Apology for a Pamphlet*, was published by [John Milton](./John_Milton "John Milton") in April 1642. It was the final of his [antiprelatical tracts](./Milton's_antiprelatical_tracts "Milton's antiprelatical tracts") which criticize the structure of the [Church of England](./Church_of_England "Church of England").

Background
----------

The *[Apology](./Apologetics "Apologetics")* was published in April 1642 as *An Apology against a Pamphlet Called a Modest Confutation of the Animadversions upon the Remonstrant against Smectymnvvs* and is [his final antiprelatical tract](./Milton's_antiprelatical_tracts "Milton's antiprelatical tracts"). The tract was written as a response to a refutation by Bishop [Joseph Hall](./Joseph_Hall_(bishop) "Joseph Hall (bishop)").[[1]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-1)

Tract
-----

Milton argues that the defense of truth makes one vulnerable to personal attacks and emphasizes that role of personal integrity, especially his own:[[2]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-2) "as a member incorporate into that truth whereof I was perswaded".[[3]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-3) Milton defends his own integrity when he later writes:[[4]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-Wheeler_p._275-4) "that indeed according to art is most eloquent, which returns and approaches neerest to nature from whence it came; and they expresse nature best, who in their lives least wander from her safe leading, which may be call'd regenerate reason".[[5]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-5) This idea is expanded further when he says:

> he who would not be frustrated of his hope to write well hereafter in laudable things, ought him selfe to bee a true Poem, that is, a composition, and patterne of the best and honourable things; not presuming to sing high praises of heroick men, or famous Cities, unlesse he have in himselfe the experience and the practice of all that which is praise-worthy.[[6]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-6)

Themes
------

The *Apology*, like many of Milton's other tracts, praises Parliament and emphasizes that they are reformers and the basis of the country.[[7]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-7) The tract also connects truth of words with the individual's character.[[4]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-Wheeler_p._275-4) Paul Stevens emphasizes that the tract reflects how "Milton's self is produced in the process of writing" and that his self is put through "a series of culturally approved *laterall* transformations".[[8]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-8) In particular, Elizabeth Wheeler points out that the tract contains "Milton's understanding of [Aristotle](./Aristotle "Aristotle")'s definition of man as a political animal. Heroism lies in the risk of changing and being changed in verbal exchange."[[9]](./Apology_for_Smectymnuus#cite_note-9)

Content:
Andraemon

In [Greek mythology](./Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](./Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](./Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](./Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](./Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](./Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](./Andraemon#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](./Andraemon#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](./Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](./Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](./Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](./Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](./Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](./Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](./Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](./Andraemon#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](./Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](./Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](./Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](./Andraemon#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](./Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](./Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](./Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](./Andraemon#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](./Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](./Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](./Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](./Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](./Andraemon#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](./Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](./Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](./Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](./Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](./Andraemon#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](./Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](./Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](./Andraemon#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](./Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](./Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](./Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](./Andraemon#cite_note-9)

Andraemon

In [Greek mythology](./Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](./Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](./Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](./Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](./Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](./Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](./Andraemon#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](./Andraemon#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](./Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](./Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](./Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](./Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](./Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](./Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](./Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](./Andraemon#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](./Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](./Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](./Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](./Andraemon#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](./Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](./Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](./Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](./Andraemon#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](./Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](./Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](./Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](./Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](./Andraemon#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](./Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](./Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](./Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](./Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](./Andraemon#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](./Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](./Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](./Andraemon#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](./Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](./Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](./Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](./Andraemon#cite_note-9)

([/ænˈdriːmən/](./Help:IPA/English \"Help:IPA/English\"); [Ancient Greek](./Ancient_Greek_language \"Ancient Greek language\"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](./Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek \"Romanization of Ancient Greek\"):\\xa0*Andraímon*) may refer to:\\n\\n* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](./Oxylus \"Oxylus\") and husband of [Dryope](./Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) \"Dryope (daughter of Dryops)\").[[1]](./Andraemon#cite_note-1)\\n* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](./Andraemon#cite_note-2)\\n* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](./Aetolia \"Aetolia\") king and husband of [Gorge](./Gorge_(mythology) \"Gorge (mythology)\") of [Calydon](./Calydon \"Calydon\"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](./Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) \"Thoas (king of Aetoila)\"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](./Oeneus \"Oeneus\")\\' power over [Aetolia](./Aetolia \"Aetolia\"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](./Amfissa \"Amfissa\").[[3]](./Andraemon#cite_note-3)\\n* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](./Leonteus_(mythology) \"Leonteus (mythology)\"). He married [Amphinome](./Amphinome \"Amphinome\"), a daughter of [Pelias](./Pelias \"Pelias\").[[4]](./Andraemon#cite_note-4)\\n* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](./Suitors_of_Penelope \"Suitors of Penelope\") of [Penelope](./Penelope \"Penelope\") who came from [Dulichium](./Dulichium \"Dulichium\") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](./Andraemon#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](./Odysseus \"Odysseus\") with the aid of [Eumaeus](./Eumaeus \"Eumaeus\"), [Philoetius](./Philoetius_(Odyssey) \"Philoetius (Odyssey)\"), and [Telemachus](./Telemachus \"Telemachus\").[[6]](./Andraemon#cite_note-6)\\n* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](./Codrus \"Codrus\"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](./Asia_Minor \"Asia Minor\") and drove the [Carians](./Caria \"Caria\") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](./Colophon_(city) \"Colophon (city)\").[[7]](./Andraemon#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](./Mimnermus \"Mimnermus\") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](./Pylos \"Pylos\") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](./Andraemon#cite_note-8)\\n\\nSimilarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](./Patronymic \"Patronymic\"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](./Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) \"Thoas (king of Aetoila)\"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](./Gorge_(mythology) \"Gorge (mythology)\").[[9]](./Andraemon#cite_note-9)\\n\\nNotes\\n-----\\n\\n* ![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ad/Parthenon_from_west.jpg/40px-Parthenon_from_west.jpg)[Ancient Greece portal](./Portal:Ancient_Greece \"Portal:Ancient Greece\")\\n* ![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e9/Draig.svg/40px-Draig.svg.png)[Myths portal](./Portal:Myths \"Portal:Myths\")\\n\\n1.
